history.dynasty: Jain monastic tradition (Bhattaraka seat); modern revival by Jain traders
history.period: Ancient tirth; ancient hill idol 1156 AD per one source vs Vikram Samvat 2418 (1361-62 AD) per another - CONFLICT (verify); Shvetambara shrine 1938; 28-ft marble statue 1963
history.summary: THIS IS A JAIN PILGRIMAGE CENTRE, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. The Bahubali Hill Temple is the Kumbhojgiri Jain tirth at Bahubali (Kumbhoj) village, Hatkanangale taluka, Kolhapur district (NOT Sangli district as the CSV suggests) - about 27-30 km from Kolhapur on the Kolhapur-Sangli highway. Both Digambara and Shvetambara sects worship here; Shvetambaras regard it as the Shatrunjaya of South Maharashtra. The hill (ancient names: Niranjangiri, Bahubalis hill, Durgadevis hill) has an ancient 6-ft Bahubali idol and temples of Shantinath, Chandaprabhu and Adinath reached by ~380-400 steps, with the moolnayak Jagvallabh Parshvanath (white marble, padmasana) in the main hill shrine. In 1816 the Bhattaraka permitted a Shvetambara installation; the Shvetambara temple was built in 1938 and the famous 28-ft monolithic marble Bahubali statue near the foothills was installed in 1963. The complex includes the Shvetambara Jahaj (ship) Mandir, models of Siddha Kshetras, a museum, dharamshala and the Bahubali Vidyapeeth Gurukul. The site is an Atishaya Kshetra (place of miracles); the Kannada poet Gunavarma II completed his Udyogsara at the Chandranatha Basadi here.

name: Bahubali Hill Temple
town: Bahubali (Kumbhoj), Hatkanangale taluka - CSV town 'Sangli' AND district are WRONG; the site is in Kolhapur district, ~30 km from Kolhapur
town_description: Bahubali (Kumbhoj) is a village in Hatkanangale taluka of Kolhapur district, about 30 km from Kolhapur and 6 km from Hatkanangale town on the Kolhapur-Sangli highway. It is best known as the home of the Kumbhojgiri Jain hill temples and the giant Bahubali statue, and is the birthplace of the social worker Padma Vibhushan Dr. Karmaveer Bhaurao Patil. The village economy blends agriculture with pilgrim services (dharamshalas, bhojanshalas, Jain hotels).

travel.railway: Hatkanangale - about 8 km; Kolhapur - about 30 km; Miraj - about 35 km (verify).
travel.road: On the Kolhapur-Sangli highway; left turn from Hatkanangale ST stand, 6 km to Kumbhoj; ~35 km from Sangli city.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; early morning or evening for the hill climb (steps get very hot midday in summer). Kartika Poornima fair is the annual gathering.
